# Error codes

Every failure carries a stable code, in snake case. With `--json`, the last line gh-touchid writes to stderr is
`{"error": {"code": "…", "message": "…"}}`; `rpc` puts the code in the error's `data.code` (with the message in
`data.message`), and `mcp` returns a tool error whose text is that same object, also under `_meta["gh-touchid/error"]`.
The message says what to run next; match on the code, not the message.

Exit status 2 means the input was wrong, so running the same thing again cannot help; 1 is any other failure, and 0
success. `gh` and `as` exit with the status of the program they ran; with `--json` they exit 0 and the output's
`exit_code` holds it.

| Code | Exit status | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `usage` | 2 | Not a gh-touchid command, or a wrong use of one; `gh-touchid help <command>` prints its usage. |
| `invalid_input` | 2 | The input does not fit the command's input schema (a field missing, unknown, of the wrong type or too large); the message names the field, and nothing was done. |
| `invalid_token` | 2 | The token on stdin is not printable ASCII without whitespace; pipe the token alone. |
| `authentication_failed` | 1 | Touch ID failed or was denied, so nothing was approved; run the command again to be asked again. |
| `approval_timed_out` | 1 | Nobody answered Touch ID in time; run the command again while someone is at the Mac. |
| `screen_locked` | 1 | The screen is locked, so nobody could approve; unlock it and run the command again. |
| `keychain` | 1 | The Keychain refused to read or store an item; the message carries the Keychain's error. |
| `missing_repository` | 1 | The command needs a repository and the current folder is not a Git repository with an origin on github.com; run it in such a clone, or name the repository where the command takes one. |
| `missing_account` | 1 | No token is stored for the account named; store one with `gh-touchid account add <login>`. |
| `missing_app` | 1 | No GitHub App is stored for the owner; make one with `gh-touchid app create <owner>`. |
| `newer_format` | 1 | A stored item was written by a newer gh-touchid, in a format this one cannot read; upgrade gh-touchid. |
| `unreadable_format` | 1 | A stored item's Keychain description names no format gh-touchid reads (it was edited?); the message names the command that stores it again. |
| `not_signed_in` | 1 | Nobody is signed in to the owner's GitHub App, or the sign-in has ended; run `gh-touchid app login <owner>`. |
| `no_app` | 1 | The repository's owner has no GitHub App stored; the message names the other ways: one of your accounts with `gh-touchid as <login> --`, or for gh the public reader. |
| `forbidden_command` | 1 | The gh command could reveal or replace the token, so gh-touchid never runs it. |
| `unknown_command` | 2 | The words name none of gh's own commands (extensions, aliases and hidden commands are not run); `gh-touchid gh --help` lists them. |
| `gh_commands_unreadable` | 1 | gh-touchid could not read gh's list of commands, which it needs to tell what a gh command does; check that this gh runs. |
| `gh_missing` | 1 | The GitHub CLI gh-touchid runs is not executable at the path the message names; reinstall gh-touchid. |
| `gh_changed` | 1 | The gh installed with gh-touchid is not the one it was built with; reinstall gh-touchid. |
| `gh_unverified` | 1 | gh-touchid could not tell which code the gh it started was running, so it stopped gh before it ran; nothing was done. |
| `unsafe_terminal_output` | 1 | `git credential get` would have written a credential to a terminal; only Git's credential pipe gets one. |
| `not_git_transport` | 1 | Something other than Git's own HTTPS transport (git-remote-https) asked for a credential, and only that transport gets one. |
| `agent` | 1 | The gh-touchid agent, which keeps sessions and elevations, failed or refused the request; the message says why. |
| `github` | 1 | GitHub refused or failed a request; the message is GitHub's answer, and running the command again can help when the failure was temporary. |
| `refused` | 1 | gh-touchid did not do what was asked (an approval not given, a callback that did not match, a file it could not open); the message says why. |
| `reader_missing` | 1 | No public reader is stored and the repository's owner has no App; run `gh-touchid reader create`, or name a repository whose owner has one. |
| `reader_not_installed` | 1 | The reader App is not installed on its owner; install it from the URL in the message. |
| `reader_installations` | 1 | The reader App is not installed exactly once, on its owner; uninstall the others on GitHub or run `gh-touchid reader remove`. |
| `reader_permissions` | 1 | The reader App has permissions, which a reader must not; remove them on GitHub or run `gh-touchid reader remove`. |
| `reader_key_rejected` | 1 | GitHub rejected the reader App's private key; store a new one with `gh-touchid reader add --app-id <id> < key.pem`. |
| `reader_exists` | 1 | A reader is already stored; give it a new key with `gh-touchid reader add`, or run `gh-touchid reader remove` first. |
| `reader_opens_issue` | 1 | The public reader cannot open issues; open one as one of your accounts with `gh-touchid as <login> -- gh issue create`. |
| `invalid_private_key` | 2 | The private key on stdin cannot be used; pipe the App's PEM key: `gh-touchid reader add --app-id <id> < key.pem`. |
| `credential_pipe_only` | 1 | `git credential` answers only Git's own credential requests, not `--json` or `--input`; Git runs it after `gh-touchid git setup <owner>`. |
| `confirmation_needed` | 2 | The command takes access away and there was no terminal to confirm on; the message gives the command that confirms with `--yes`. |
| `input_needed` | 2 | The command needs an answer and could not ask (`--no-input`, or no terminal); the message gives the commands that do it without asking. |
| `adapter_missing` | 1 | `rpc` and `mcp` need gh-touchid-adapter, which is missing or not executable; reinstall gh-touchid. |
| `output_invalid` | 1 | The command ran, but its result does not fit its declared output schema; this is a bug in gh-touchid, so report it with the message. |
| `error` | 1 | A failure the system reported that has no code of its own; the message says what failed. |

## The adapter's own codes

`rpc` and `mcp` run through gh-touchid-adapter, which reports the core's codes as they are and adds two of its own
([CoreCall.swift](../Sources/GHTouchIDAdapter/CoreCall.swift),
[Catalog.swift](../Sources/GHTouchIDAdapter/Catalog.swift)):

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `adapter` | The adapter could not run gh-touchid, or gh-touchid said nothing it could read; check that gh-touchid runs (`gh-touchid --help --json`). |
| `secret_needs_stdin` | The tool takes a secret, which only standard input may carry; run the command the message names in a terminal, with the secret piped in. |

## JSON-RPC error numbers

`rpc` answers a failed request with a JSON-RPC 2.0 error whose `code` is one of these numbers, and whose `data` is
`{"code", "message"}`: gh-touchid's or the adapter's code, or for a request the adapter refuses itself, one of its own
([RPCServer.swift](../Sources/GHTouchIDAdapter/RPCServer.swift)).

| Number | `data.code` | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| -32700 | `parse_error` | A line that is not JSON; the server reads on. |
| -32600 | `invalid_request` | A message that is not a JSON-RPC request, or reuses the id of a call still running. |
| -32601 | `method_not_found` | A method that names no operation. |
| -32602 | `invalid_params` | Params that are not a JSON object. |
| -32602 | gh-touchid's | gh-touchid refused the input (exit status 2). |
| -32000 | gh-touchid's, or `secret_needs_stdin` | Any other failure of gh-touchid, and the adapter's refusal of a secret. |
| -32603 | `adapter` | gh-touchid could not run, or said nothing the adapter could read. |
| -32800 | `cancelled` | The client cancelled the request (as in LSP). |
